title: The Judge Is Not Impartial: Self-Preference in Medical LLM Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2611.18616v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate model-generated medical content, creating a potential circularity: an LLM judge may favor outputs generated by the same model independently of clinical quality. To characterize LLM judge self-preference in medical settings, we measured same-model affinity in single-turn specialist question answering and multi-turn standardized-patient encounters. We evaluated eight models, two from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Qwen, on 620 real point of care questions from clinicians (Real-POCQi). The same eight models also generated and judged 200 standardized patient-clinician scenarios (MedSP1000) up to 8 visible turns. In total, our analysis spans 13,760 LLM judgments. We define three complementary measures of self-preference. Answer Rank Bias, our primary measure, compared the rank assigned to a fixed response by its own-model judge with its average rank from outside judges. Answer S

translated_title: 评判者并非公正无私：医学大语言模型评估中的自我偏好
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于评估模型生成的医学内容，这带来了一个潜在的循环性问题：LLM评判者可能会偏爱由同一模型生成的输出，而与其临床质量无关。为了刻画医学场景中LLM评判者的自我偏好，我们测量了单轮专科问答和多轮标准化患者诊疗对话中的同模型亲和度。我们使用来自临床医生的620个真实诊疗点问题，评估了八个模型（分别来自OpenAI、Anthropic、Google和Qwen各两个）。同样的八个模型还生成并评判了200个标准化患者-临床医生场景（MedSP1000），最多包含8个可见轮次。总计，我们的分析涵盖了13,760次LLM评判。我们定义了三种互补的自我偏好度量方法。其中，答案排名偏差作为我们的主要度量方法，将同一模型评判者对固定回答所赋予的排名与其来自外部评判者的平均排名进行比较。（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过13,760次LLM评判系统量化了医学评估场景中的“自我偏好”现象，发现LLM评判者会偏向同一模型生成的输出而与其临床质量无关，揭示了使用LLM评判医学内容时存在的循环性偏差风险。
en_tdlr: This study systematically quantifies self-preference in medical LLM evaluation through 13,760 LLM judgments, showing that LLM judges favor outputs generated by the same model independently of clinical quality, revealing a circularity bias when using LLMs to evaluate medical content.
